paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: greatness is a gift, and the Giver is not the one holding it. God tells us Assyria's cedar grew tall because "The waters made it grow; the deep springs made it tall" (Ezekiel 31:4). He even says, "I made it beautiful with its many branches" (Ezekiel 31:9). So when you're tall, blessed or admired, somebody else watered that tree.

The trouble starts when the tree forgets. "It grew proud on account of its height" (Ezekiel 31:10), and pride is where the whole fall begins. Then God turns to Pharaoh and asks, "Who then is like you in glory and greatness among the trees of Eden?" (Ezekiel 31:18). I think that question is a mirror, because Pharaoh is looking at a tree that fell and is being asked if he sees himself.

So here's what I'm taking to the bakery today. Whatever God has given you, hold it with open hands, and give Him the thanks. Nobody has ever stood too humble to be lifted, and nobody has ever stood so high that God couldn't see the top. Stay close to the water, baker, and remember who sent the rain.
